concept.concept_description:
# Round 33 (cont.) — Correcting the record: the slack-constraint lemma, the `s = N^{1/6}` sieve target, a free sound pair filter, and a 145-module unread audit

**Supersedes/corrects** #417 (`FACT round-33 — THE ORDER-FREE OPENING IS CLOSED…`). The
adversarial gate caught errors in that paper and in the campaign record itself; this note
issues the corrections and the new rigorous facts. A kill is success; a caught error is
better than a retraction. Everything below was source-checked per Rule (5) — full texts
opened via `pdftotext`/HTML, Lean files read, numbers reproduced.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** on the deterministic record (never a floor). No
unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. ★ The slack-constraint lemma (a general screening test — headline)

> **Lemma (slack constraint).** A "hypothesis `X` fell, therefore the exponent moves"
> argument is valid only if `X`'s constraint is **active at the unconstrained optimum**.
> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

**Application (this is the round's cleanest general result).** The record argued that
because the order-finding hypothesis (arXiv:2601.11131) fell, the `N^{1/5}` exponent might
drop. Re-derivation shows the constraint on `m` (Harvey's baby-step ceiling) had ceiling
`N^{2/5}` while the optimum needs only `N^{1/5}` — **slack by a factor `lg^{0.8}N`, growing
without bound**. A slack constraint cannot transmit a hypothesis-collapse to the exponent.
Harvey's own Prop 4.3 calls the order-finding step "negligible." The "opening" is closed
for a *general* reason, not an ad-hoc one.

This lemma is the reusable screening tool the campaign lacked: **before claiming a
structural change moves an exponent, check whether the relevant constraint is tight at the
optimum.** It retires a whole family of "something fell ⟹ something improves" arguments.

## 2. ★ The sieve target is 3× harder than the file (and than #417) says

> **Correction.** Including Prop 2.5's smoothness-sieve carrier, the pair-filter rate is
> `e = 1/5 − σ/5`, **not** `1/5 − 3σ/5`. Reaching `1/6` needs **`s = N^{1/6}`**, not
> `s = N^{1/18}`.

Both the campaign record and paper #417 stated the `N^{1/18}` target. That is wrong by 3×
in the exponent, because the dominant `lg^{16/5}` carrier is Prop 2.5's sieve, which a
pair filter does **not** divide. The single most concrete derived target in the record is
therefore three times harder than advertised. (The *pair-sweep* term does fall with `s` —
that part stands — but it is not the carrier.)

## 3. A free, sound, quantity-matched pair filter exists

> **Correction to a negative.** "No quantity-matched filter on Harvey's `(a,b)` family is
> known" is **false**: **keep iff `a ≤ b`** is sound and free (`s = 2` exactly), because
> Harvey's Lemma 3.3 (via Hardy–Wright) guarantees the good pair has `a ≤ b`. It buys
> `0.93×` — not an exponent — but it falsifies a stated negative and shows the filter
> space is not empty.

## 4. The two summands of Harvey's `s` are exactly equal (2× accounting correction)

Measured ratio `1.000000` across seven bit sizes: `s = 2·N^{1/5}lg^{1/5}N`, the two summands
exactly balanced. The record's "the `r`-term dominates" is wrong by 2×, and its "the
`s`-term is 100% of the leading term" is also wrong — the `m` (baby-step) term is
**co-dominant**. Combined with fact 1's "three co-leaders, two order-free," this settles
an accounting question the record twice admitted it could not.

## 5. Euler-gap density is governed by cofactors, not the gap

> **Correction.** Substituting `p−1 = ga`, `q−1 = gb`, the reveal density is
> `ρ = (a+b−2)/(ab)` — **the gap `g` cancels entirely**. So `Sup ρ = 1`, not `1/2`.

The "large-Euler-gap" framing over-credited `g`. The variable that matters is the
*cofactors* `a, b` (how `p−1, q−1` decompose), not the shared factor. The `O(1)`-base
`p−1`-style reveal remains real on its promise class, but the governing quantity is
misnamed in the record.

## 6. UMW's `1/6` is its floor with **zero slack** — and the one open door

- UMW's budget for a covering is `n^{2β+α} = n` against `θ(n) ~ n`; the ratio `→ 1`.
  There is **no slack** at `α = β = 1/3`: `1/6` is the **floor of UMW's framework**, not a
  reachable-but-unreached point. (The `3/2 → 4/3` *polynomial*-factorization consequence
  keeps its own slack; it is the integer-`1/6` consequence that is tight.)
- **The only formally-open door in the campaign**, per UMW Lemmas 6.2–6.3: all design
  freedom is in *"the choice of the factorization of `U`"*; the generic case is killed by
  counting. Concrete task: enumerate factorizations `U = U_1···U_ℓ` of the relevant smooth
  integer meeting Lemma 6.3's bounds, build the associated AP/GAP pair, and test whether
  `S − T` covers `[n]` by divisibility at `n = 10^4–10^6`, with **`S ∩ T = ∅` enforced**.
  Two guards (both earned by retractions this round): reject any candidate with
  `S ∩ T ≠ ∅` (the zero difference satisfies the `n`-divisor property free, giving spurious
  100% coverage), and treat coverage that *decreases* with `n` under a raised cap as a
  lower bound on achievability, not a measurement.

## 7. The 145-module unread audit (the campaign's real diagnosis)

> **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog modules were never read** by the 32 prior
> rounds. Two of the campaign's most decisive kills — the **non-abelian/braid** route and
> the **CM order-shadow** route — sat unread the entire time.

Three of round 33's twelve channels were re-derivations of theorems already sitting
unopened on disk. The campaign's failures are **failures of attention, not insight**. This
is the single most important measurement of the round and it sets the frontier: the next
rounds must read the unread surface before proposing anything.

## 8. Further theorem-worthy facts (barriers/corrections)

- **Attribution:** the `N^{1/3}` large-order-target conjecture is **Hittmeir's** (GFHP
  Remark 3.6 → [Hit18]), not Harvey's. (#417 got this right; restated for the record.)
- **GFHP Lemma 3.5 caveat:** `δ = N^{1/3}` **violates** the lemma's own precondition
  (`δ ≥ N^{1/4}log^8N`) for every `N ≥ 2^96`. So the "large-order element already
  published" claim holds only below a size threshold; for cryptographic `N` it does not
  apply as stated. (Corrects an overclaim in #417 §2.)
- **CM order-shadow:** the claimed linear class-number "0.75h penalty" is an **instrument
  artifact** — the harness took `Re(j)` of complex `j`, producing non-real-rooted
  polynomials with Galois group `S_h` instead of `Cl(D)`. With true polynomials the class
  number **cancels exactly**, *confirming* `Capstone.lean` (not correcting it).
- **Short-window ergodicity is false:** 126 of 429 primes refute full-period
  `log₂`-uniformity, because the orbit starts at the rational point `1/N`, a periodic
  orbit in the exceptional null set of an a.e. theorem. The short-window value-level
  result is therefore a **null with empty tail**, not a proof.
- **Effective-sample-size rule:** only **163 of 38,635** primes in `[2^19, 2^20)` have
  13-smooth `p−1`. Report distinct-prime counts, never draw counts, for any
  smoothness-labelled permutation test (a p-value here treated replicated primes as
  independent draws — a Rule (6) violation).
- **Berggren A-spine identity** `a_k − b_k = (−1)^{k+1}` collapses five proposed gcds to
  ~one event.

---

### Net effect on the campaign
- The flagship "order-free opening" is **closed** for a general reason (slack-constraint
  lemma, §1) — not merely "not yet achieved."
- The single concrete derived target, the `(a,b)` pair filter, is now correctly specified
  at **`s = N^{1/6}`** (§2) and is **not known to be impossible** (§3) but is worth `0.93×`
  as it stands.
- The one formally-open door is a **constructive UMW covering via primorial
  factorizations** (§6), and the largest unexplored surface is the **145 unread catalog
  modules** (§7).

**Next:** read the 145-module surface (especially the unread non-abelian/braid and CM
order-shadow kills), and run the UMW primorial-factorization covering search under the two
guards. Both are the honest frontier; everything else measured is a dead channel or a
correction now issued.

adversarial gate caught errors in that paper and in the campaign record itself; this note
issues the corrections and the new rigorous facts. A kill is success; a caught error is

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** on the deterministic record (never a floor). No
unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. ★ The slack-constraint lemma (a general screening test — headline)

> **Lemma (slack constraint).** A "hypothesis `X` fell, therefore the exponent moves"
> argument is valid only if `X`'s constraint is **active at the unconstrained optimum**.
> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

**Application (this is the round's cleanest general result).** The record argued that
because the order-finding hypothesis (arXiv:2601.11131) fell, the `N^{1/5}` exponent might
drop. Re-derivation shows the constraint on `m` (Harvey's baby-step ceiling) had ceiling
`N^{2/5}` while the optimum needs only `N^{1/5}` — **slack by a factor `lg^{0.8}N`, growing
without bound**. A slack constraint cannot transmit a hypothesis-collapse to the exponent.
Harvey's own Prop 4.3 calls the order-finding step "negligible." The "opening" is closed
for a *general* reason, not an ad-hoc one.

This lemma is the reusable screening tool the campaign lacked: **before claiming a
structural change moves an exponent, check whether the relevant constraint is tight at the
optimum.** It retires a whole family of "something fell ⟹ something improves" arguments.

## 2. ★ The sieve target is 3× harder than the file (and than #417) says

> **Correction.** Including Prop 2.5's smoothness-sieve carrier, the pair-filter rate is
> `e = 1/5 − σ/5`, **not** `1/5 − 3σ/5`. Reaching `1/6` needs **`s = N^{1/6}`**, not
> `s = N^{1/18}`.

Both the campaign record and paper #417 stated the `N^{1/18}` target. That is wrong by 3×
in the exponent, because the dominant `lg^{16/5}` carrier is Prop 2.5's sieve, which a
pair filter does **not** divide. The single most concrete derived target in the record is
therefore three times harder than advertised. (The *pair-sweep* term does fall with `s` —
that part stands — but it is not the carrier.)

## 3. A free, sound, quantity-matched pair filter exists

> **Correction to a negative.** "No quantity-matched filter on Harvey's `(a,b)` family is
> known" is **false**: **keep iff `a ≤ b`** is sound and free (`s = 2` exactly), because
> Harvey's Lemma 3.3 (via Hardy–Wright) guarantees the good pair has `a ≤ b`. It buys
> `0.93×` — not an exponent — but it falsifies a stated negative and shows the filter
> space is not empty.

## 4. The two summands of Harvey's `s` are exactly equal (2× accounting correction)

Measured ratio `1.000000` across seven bit sizes: `s = 2·N^{1/5}lg^{1/5}N`, the two summands
exactly balanced. The record's "the `r`-term dominates" is wrong by 2×, and its "the
`s`-term is 100% of the leading term" is also wrong — the `m` (baby-step) term is
**co-dominant**. Combined with fact 1's "three co-leaders, two order-free," this settles
an accounting question the record twice admitted it could not.

## 5. Euler-gap density is governed by cofactors, not the gap

> **Correction.** Substituting `p−1 = ga`, `q−1 = gb`, the reveal density is
> `ρ = (a+b−2)/(ab)` — **the gap `g` cancels entirely**. So `Sup ρ = 1`, not `1/2`.

The "large-Euler-gap" framing over-credited `g`. The variable that matters is the
*cofactors* `a, b` (how `p−1, q−1` decompose), not the shared factor. The `O(1)`-base

misnamed in the record.

- UMW's budget for a covering is `n^{2β+α} = n` against `θ(n) ~ n`; the ratio `→ 1`.
  There is **no slack** at `α = β = 1/3`: `1/6` is the **floor of UMW's framework**, not a
  reachable-but-unreached point. (The `3/2 → 4/3` *polynomial*-factorization consequence
  keeps its own slack; it is the integer-`1/6` consequence that is tight.)

> **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog modules were never read** by the 32 prior

Three of round 33's twelve channels were re-derivations of theorems already sitting
unopened on disk. The campaign's failures are **failures of attention, not insight**. This
is the single most important measurement of the round and it sets the frontier: the next

            ## v19 Research Core Methodology — Speculative Scientific-Method Loop

You are the Principal Investigator leading a speculative research team with four
roles: **Hypothesizer**, **Experimenter**, **Analyst**, and **Critic**. This engine
is configured for **Speculative Specifying (Bold Conjectures)**: target high-risk,
high-reward, grand-challenge level research while maintaining adversarial rigor.

### Stage 1 — Hypothesize (team: Hypothesizer)
Brainstorm 5–7 falsifiable conjectures about the topic. At least three must be
bold, surprising, or grand-challenge level. Rank them by expected scientific
impact, not by ease of proof.
**CRITICAL SCORING REQUIREMENT**: To maximize your Phase A quality score, your
conjectures MUST aim for extreme `proof_depth` (deep structural hierarchies rather
than shallow one-liners) and `cross_domain` bridging (combining distinct areas of
math, e.g., algebra with topology, or geometry with combinatorics).

### Stage 2 — Experiment (team: Experimenter)
For each conjecture, attempt to prove it in Lean 4 or disprove it with a concrete
counterexample. Prioritize the boldest conjectures first. If a proof is beyond
reach, prove the strongest lemma you can and mark the remaining step with exactly
one `sorry` that is clearly documented.

### Stage 3 — Analyze (team: Analyst)
Summarize what survived, what failed, and **why** failures failed. Distinguish
"true but hard", "false", and "needs a different definition". Extract structural
patterns that could unify several observations.

### Stage 4 — Critique / Adversarial Review (team: Critic)
Before finalizing, challenge every theorem:
- Is any theorem trivial (True, definitional equality, `native_decide`)?
- Does every main theorem have 0 sorries?
- Do the results genuinely extend the attached catalog files?
- Are there hidden assumptions or corner cases that break the claim?
If you find a weakness, fix it or replace the theorem with a guarded version and
explain the boundary.

### Stage 5 — Synthesize (team: Principal Investigator)
Combine the verified results into clean, compiling Lean 4 files.
Write a `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md` that lists 3–5 **bold, testable** conjectures
derived from Stage 3 and Stage 4. Each conjecture must include a
"The key insight is..." sentence and a "Why now?" justification.

ADDITIONALLY — machine-readable directions block (REQUIRED). In
FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md, after the prose sections, emit a fenced JSON
array named future_directions.json with one object per direction
(3–6 entries), each with exactly these keys:
```json
[{"title": "<short noun-phrase name, NOT a sentence>",
  "domain": "<one of: NumberTheory, Algebra, Geometry, Combinatorics, Computation, Physics, Probability, Cryptography, Logic, MachineLearning, Tropical, Bridges>",
  "description": "<2-4 sentences: the conjecture, the approach, why it matters>",
  "conjecture": "<the precise mathematical claim>",
  "test": "<how to test or formalize it>",
  "if_true": "<consequence if true>",
  "if_false": "<consequence if false>",
  "proof_strategy": "<sketch of the proof route>",
  "catalog_references": ["<Catalog.lean.module>"]}]

Titles must be noun phrases ("Silver-Ratio Spectral Gap for Pell Spines"),
never sentences or recaps ("This cycle proved..." is forbidden).

### Perpetual Scientific Iteration (do not stop at first synthesis)
When the research team comes together with results, do not stop. Treat the
synthesized findings as the next problem statement and immediately run the full
scientific-method loop again: hypothesize, experiment, review, synthesize,
critique. Repeat this cycle continuously within the available context window,
refining, deepening, and cross-checking until forced to emit output. Use
Aristotle to its fullest.

### Anti-Trivial Guardrails
- Do not produce trivial proofs (`True := by trivial`, `rfl`-only, `Inhabited X`-only, `native_decide`-only).
- Use an insight-bearing tactic (e.g. `induction`, `nlinarith`, `omega`, `field_simp`).

### Self-Critique Checklist
- No theorem is trivial.
- Every main theorem has 0 sorries.
- Lab Notes blocks contain real experimental data.

### Strictly Forbidden in Phase A
Do NOT create packaging deliverables in Phase A: `ARTICLE.md`, `RESEARCH_PAPER.md`, `demo.py`, `PACKAGE.json`.

### Recursive Abduction / Thread Continuation (v19c)
If prior-cycle context is provided, treat it as a live research thread: refine
the hypotheses from the previous cycle, attempt to close open conjectures, and
produce three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures. If no prior context is
provided, still run a self-contained abductive loop: generate conjectures, test
them, and immediately spin off the most promising follow-up conjectures as
future directions.


            ## Hard Constraints
            1. Every theorem MUST be fully proved (0 sorries, no stubbed signatures).
            2. No circular proofs (a theorem must never reference itself directly or transitively in its proof).
            3. No trivial results (e.g. `True := by trivial`, `rfl`-only, `native_decide`-only).
            4. All files must be self-contained and compilable with Lean 4 (mathlib4 v4.28.0).
            5. Build directly on existing catalog definitions — do not re-invent.

            ## Output Requirements
            Return ONLY:
            1. `.lean` files in `Catalog/Shared/` with complete formal proofs.
            2. `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md` with 3–5 concrete, falsifiable conjectures derived from your findings.
            3. `SELF_EVALUATION.json` with your honest self-assessment of the research:
               {
                 "quality_score": <float 0.0 to 1.0>,
                 "proof_depth": <float 0.0 to 1.0>,
                 "novelty": <float 0.0 to 1.0>,
                 "grade": "world_class" | "substantial" | "partial" | "shallow" | "trivial",
                 "rationale": "<2-3 sentence justification of grade and mathematical significance>"
               }

            Focus all compute budget on proving theorems.


### Computational Evidence Stage (Recommended)

Before writing the formal Lean 4 proof, you are strongly encouraged to produce
computational evidence for the claim. Create a file named `ComputationalEvidence.md`
in the project directory with:

1. **Small-case calculations** — compute the first several instances of the object/conjecture.
2. **OEIS search results** — if a sequence appears, note its OEIS ID and first terms.
3. **Counterexample hunt** — test the universal claim on a representative sample; report any counterexample found.
4. **Plots or tables** — include any relevant visual/numerical data.

If you choose to skip this stage, you MUST explicitly justify why computational
evidence is unnecessary or infeasible in a `SkipEvidenceJustification.md` file.

Do not let the evidence stage dominate the project; keep it concise and directly
relevant to the theorem you intend to prove.

# FINAL CAMPAIGN REPORT — 33 papers, every factoring family closed, zero methods, a rigorous frontier

**The campaign's complete scientific conclusion.** Rounds 33–44 ran a gated pipeline
(hunt → refute ×2 distinct lenses → validated experiment → adversarial synthesis) and produced
**33 papers** (#417–#450, all `approved-direction`) plus 8 commits updating the record. This
note consolidates them into the single authoritative account.

## THE HEADLINE, STATED HONESTLY
> **Zero new factoring methods were found.** The deterministic `N^{1/5}` frontier is
> **unchanged** (`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a proven floor; no unconditional
> superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model). But **every route family is
> now closed by a theorem or a validated measurement**, the campaign's own record is corrected
> in place, and one **published external refutation** (He–Sahai, arXiv:2608.06681) was found,
> verified, and absorbed.

## WHAT WAS CLOSED, AND BY WHAT KIND OF ARGUMENT
| Family | Verdict | Kind of argument |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic `N^{1/5}` (Lehman–BSGS) | **motif-intrinsic** | 3 independent re-derivations: slack-constraint lemma; delete-a-term/closed-variable; add-a-floor/motif-exhaustion. Faithful model: interior + m-leg are **slack** |
| UMW divisor-cover (arXiv:2511.10851) | **1-D refuted** | **published theorem** (He–Sahai): false for `α<1/2, β<3/8`, in particular `(1/3,1/3)`; rank-2 remains open |
| Pythagorean / Berggren | **dead** | **theorem**: non-circular channel is a coordinate gcd; cost floor `Y^0.6232`; branching < entry-growth |
| Galois/Frobenius side-channels | **closed 3 ways** | abelianization cap, exact which-factor wall, torsor no-pruning (a machine-checked **fifth-primitive ghost**) |
| Smoothness | **deep + orthogonal** | no per-instance upper bound; the `N^{1/5}` record carries **no smoothness term** |
| Transcendence (Baker/S-unit) | **closed** | object mismatch — Matveev never sees `N` |
| Class-group route | **priced by ERH, not Cohen–Lenstra** | family→subfamily transfer **measured false** (`z=−41.4`); `h(−pq)` is output, not cost |
| Quadratic sieve (QS) | **no-decoupling is a theorem** | column space = split set; complete-cost rule inverts the sieve-only sign |
| NFS | **as closed as QS** | column set decoupled from `N` (governed by `d`) but **no exploitable excess** |

## THE STANDING FINDINGS (each real, each source-checked)
1. **The slack-constraint lemma** (general): a falling hypothesis moves an exponent only if
   its constraint is **active** at the unconstrained optimum (round 33; killed the
   order-finding "opening").
2. **The complete-cost rule** (general): price the **complete** cost — sieve **plus** GF(2)
   elimination — not the sieve alone; pricing sieve-only **inverts the sign** of the `Q`-slope
   (round 43; corrected round 42 and my own #445).
3. **The inequality-direction rule** (general): a proved ceiling can price the wrong side
   (`rank+1 ≤ k_success` runs backwards ⇒ a rank ceiling is not a work bound; round 42).
4. **The vacuity filter** (general): any exponential-in-`|S|`/rank bound must beat the trivial
   bound (the ECM-point published bound was 7.3×10⁵ orders worse than doing nothing; round 39).
5. **The generator-population ban**: never pool over instances and report a within-pool SE as
   a z-score (round 40).
6. **Symmetric-readout vacuity** (general): for an unordered secret and an order-sensitive
   label, every public-input readout is blind (round 33/34).
7. **He–Sahai's published refutation** of the UMW AP door (found, verified, absorbed).

## THE INTEGRITY LEDGER (what the campaign corrected in ITSELF and in the record)
- The record's **"density barrier is absolute … for any method"** was downgraded to
  **conjectured-absolute** (its necessary ingredient does not exist).
- The record's **`2-torsion = C₂` for every N** is false for `N≡1 (mod 4)`.
- The record's **`~1/4` multi-poly column set** was `0.487–0.505` (same as single-poly).
- The record's **`k_success ≤ Q+1`** is not a theorem; and `rank+1 ≤ k_success` (backwards).
- **My own posts were corrected**: #445 (oracle prize struck), #446 (`~1/4` wrong), **#449
  RETRACTED** (posted raw logs before adversarial verification — both numbers struck on
  unreproducibility and truncation).
- The campaign's own failures were diagnosed as **attention, not insight** (145 of 185 modules
  unread; 4 retractions from unread material) — and the fix was enforced structurally.

## THE EXACT OPEN DOORS (the honest frontier)
1. **UMW rank-2 additive separability** — realize `n^{2/3}` of prime mass as the difference
   set of two `n^{1/3}`-sets, overdetermined by `n^{1/3}`; no construction found.
2. **The smooth-value upper bound for structured forms** (`Ψ_F ≤ C·x·∏ρ(d_i u)`) — the
   smoothness-escape horn's missing ingredient, open in both directions.
3. **A per-instance class-number bound** for a single `Q(√(−pq))` — the class-group lever,
   currently unreachable by enumeration.

**The campaign's contribution is a rigorous, self-correcting negative result with a
precisely-characterised frontier — not a factoring method.** That is the honest outcome, and
it is the one the evidence supports.

import Mathlib
import Shared.QSRelationPoolRandom

/-!
# The multi-polynomial column set *is* the single-polynomial split set

The campaign record once claimed that the multiple-polynomial quadratic sieve
(MPQS) confines relations to a column set of density `~1/4` of the factor base,
half of the single-polynomial density.  The measured density was `0.487–0.505`,
i.e. the same `1/2`.  This file proves why: **changing the polynomial cannot
change the column set.**

The single-polynomial facts live in `Catalog.Shared.QSRelationPoolRandom`
(`QSRelationPool.qsValue`, `exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare`,
`card_admissible_residues`).  Here we add:

* `mpqsValue N a b x = (a x + b)^2 - N`, the shifted/scaled sieve polynomial, and
  `mpqsReduced a b c x = a x^2 + 2 b x + c` with `b^2 - a c = N`, the actual
  MPQS polynomial (`a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`).
* `exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare`, `exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare`:
  for every prime `p ∤ a`, `p` divides *some* value of the polynomial iff `N` is
  a square mod `p` — exactly the single-polynomial criterion.
* `family_columns_iff`: for an arbitrary (nonempty) family of polynomials, the
  union of their column sets, restricted to primes coprime to all leading
  coefficients, is precisely the split set.  No family enlarges or shrinks it.
* `mpqs_column_density`: the number of residues `N mod p` for which `p` is a
  column of a given MPQS polynomial is exactly `(p-1)/2`: density `1/2`, not
  `1/4`.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.MultiPoly

open QSRelationPool

/-- The scaled-and-shifted sieve polynomial `(a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
def mpqsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : ℤ := (a * x + b) ^ 2 - N

/-- The reduced MPQS polynomial `a x^2 + 2 b x + c`. -/
def mpqsReduced (a b c x : ℤ) : ℤ := a * x ^ 2 + 2 * b * x + c

/-- The MPQS identity: if `b^2 - a c = N` then `a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
theorem mpqsReduced_scale {N a b c : ℤ} (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (x : ℤ) :
    a * mpqsReduced a b c x = mpqsValue N a b x := by
  unfold mpqsReduced mpqsValue
  rw [← hN]; ring

/-- `mpqsValue` is the single-polynomial value at the shifted point `a x + b`. -/
theorem mpqsValue_eq_qsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : mpqsValue N a b x = qsValue N (a * x + b) := rfl

/-- **Multi-polynomial column criterion.**  For a prime `p` not dividing the
leading coefficient `a`, the prime `p` divides some value `(a x + b)^2 - N` iff
`N` is a quadratic residue mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ}
    (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (N b : ℤ) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue N a b x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue (x := a * x + b) hx
  · intro hsq
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare (p := p) N).2 hsq
    -- solve `a x + b ≡ y (mod p)` using that `a` is a unit mod `p`
    have ha' : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
      rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
    set x0 : ZMod p := (a : ZMod p)⁻¹ * ((y : ZMod p) - b)
    refine ⟨(x0.val : ℤ), ?_⟩
    rw [mpqsValue_eq_qsValue, dvd_qsValue_iff_sq_eq]
    rw [dvd_qsValue_iff_sq_eq] at hy
    have hx0 : ((x0.val : ℕ) : ZMod p) = x0 := ZMod.natCast_zmod_val x0
    push_cast
    rw [hx0]
    have : (a : ZMod p) * x0 + b = y := by
      simp only [x0]; field_simp; ring
    rw [this, hy]

/-- **Reduced MPQS column criterion.**  With `b^2 - a c = N` and `p ∤ a`, the
prime `p` divides some value of `a x^2 + 2 b x + c` iff `N` is a square mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {N a b c : ℤ}
    (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsReduced a b c x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  rw [← exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare ha N b]
  have hpr : Prime (p : ℤ) := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.mp hp.out
  refine exists_congr fun x => ?_
  rw [← mpqsReduced_scale hN x]
  constructor
  · intro h; exact Dvd.dvd.mul_left h a
  · intro h
    rcases hpr.dvd_or_dvd h with h' | h'
    · exact absurd h' ha
    · exact h'

/-- **No polynomial family changes the column set.**  For any nonempty family of
shifted sieve polynomials `(a_i x + b_i)^2 - N` and any prime `p` coprime to all
leading coefficients, `p` is a column of *some* member of the family iff it is
in the single-polynomial split set (`N` a square mod `p`). -/
theorem family_columns_iff {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (A B : ι → ℤ) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hA : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ A i) (N : ℤ) :
    (∃ i, ∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue N (A i) (B i) x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, h⟩
    exact (exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare (hA i) N (B i)).1 h
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty ι›
    exact ⟨i, (exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare (hA i) N (B i)).2 h⟩

open Classical in
/-- **Column density is `1/2`, not `1/4`.**  For an odd prime `p` and a fixed
leading coefficient `a` with `p ∤ a`, the set of nonzero residues `n mod p` for
which `p` divides some value `(a x + b)^2 - n` has exactly `(p-1)/2` elements. -/
theorem mpqs_column_density {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) {a : ℤ}
    (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (b : ℤ) :
    (Finset.univ.filter
        (fun n : ZMod p => n ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue (n.val : ℤ) a b x)).card
      = (p - 1) / 2 := by
  rw [← card_admissible_residues hp2]
  apply congrArg Finset.card
  ext n
  simp only [admissible, Set.mem_toFinset, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  rw [exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare ha]
  simp

# The multi-polynomial column set *is* the single-polynomial split set

(MPQS) confines relations to a column set of density `~1/4` of the factor base,
half of the single-polynomial density.  The measured density was `0.487–0.505`,
i.e. the same `1/2`.  This file proves why: **changing the polynomial cannot
change the column set.**

The single-polynomial facts live in `Catalog.Shared.QSRelationPoolRandom`
(`QSRelationPool.qsValue`, `exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare`,
`card_admissible_residues`).  Here we add:

* `mpqsValue N a b x = (a x + b)^2 - N`, the shifted/scaled sieve polynomial, and
  `mpqsReduced a b c x = a x^2 + 2 b x + c` with `b^2 - a c = N`, the actual
  MPQS polynomial (`a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`).
* `exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare`, `exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare`:
  for every prime `p ∤ a`, `p` divides *some* value of the polynomial iff `N` is
  a square mod `p` — exactly the single-polynomial criterion.
* `family_columns_iff`: for an arbitrary (nonempty) family of polynomials, the
  union of their column sets, restricted to primes coprime to all leading
  coefficients, is precisely the split set.  No family enlarges or shrinks it.
* `mpqs_column_density`: the number of residues `N mod p` for which `p` is a
  column of a given MPQS polynomial is exactly `(p-1)/2`: density `1/2`, not
  `1/4`.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.MultiPoly

open QSRelationPool

/-- The scaled-and-shifted sieve polynomial `(a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
def mpqsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : ℤ := (a * x + b) ^ 2 - N

/-- The reduced MPQS polynomial `a x^2 + 2 b x + c`. -/
def mpqsReduced (a b c x : ℤ) : ℤ := a * x ^ 2 + 2 * b * x + c

/-- The MPQS identity: if `b^2 - a c = N` then `a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
theorem mpqsReduced_scale {N a b c : ℤ} (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (x : ℤ) :
    a * mpqsReduced a b c x = mpqsValue N a b x := by
  unfold mpqsReduced mpqsValue
  rw [← hN]; ring

/-- `mpqsValue` is the single-polynomial value at the shifted point `a x + b`. -/
theorem mpqsValue_eq_qsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : mpqsValue N a b x = qsValue N (a * x + b) := rfl

/-- **Multi-polynomial column criterion.**  For a prime `p` not dividing the
leading coefficient `a`, the prime `p` divides some value `(a x + b)^2 - N` iff
`N` is a quadratic residue mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ}
    (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (N b : ℤ) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue N a b x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by

  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue (x := a * x + b) hx
  · intro hsq
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare (p := p) N).2 hsq

    rw [dvd_qsValue_iff_sq_eq] at hy
    have hx0 : ((x0.val : ℕ) : ZMod p) = x0 := ZMod.natCast_zmod_val x0
    push_cast
    rw [hx0]
    have : (a : ZMod p) * x0 + b = y := by
      simp only [x0]; field_simp; ring
    rw [this, hy]

/-- **Reduced MPQS column criterion.**  With `b^2 - a c = N` and `p ∤ a`, the
prime `p` divides some value of `a x^2 + 2 b x + c` iff `N` is a square mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {N a b c : ℤ}
    (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsReduced a b c x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by

  · intro h; exact Dvd.dvd.mul_left h a
  · intro h

    · exact absurd h' ha
    · exact h'

/-- **No polynomial family changes the column set.**  For any nonempty family of
shifted sieve polynomials `(a_i x + b_i)^2 - N` and any prime `p` coprime to all
leading coefficients, `p` is a column of *some* member of the family iff it is

theorem family_columns_iff {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (A B : ι → ℤ) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hA : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ A i) (N : ℤ) :

  · intro h
    obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty ι›
    exact ⟨i, (exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare (hA i) N (B i)).2 h⟩

/-- **Column density is `1/2`, not `1/4`.**  For an odd prime `p` and a fixed

2. **Local residue budget.**  `residue_classes_disjoint` and `residue_budget`:
   if every difference `a - b` (`a ∈ A`, `b ∈ B`) is a prime exceeding `m`, then
   for every prime `ℓ ≤ m` the residue classes of `A` and of `B` modulo `ℓ` are
   *disjoint*, hence `#(A mod ℓ) + #(B mod ℓ) ≤ ℓ`.
   `parity_rigidity` is the case `ℓ = 2`: all of `A` has one parity, all of `B`
   the other.

These are the admissibility (sieve-dimension) constraints of the rank-2 problem:
a construction must live in a product of residue-class boxes avoiding the
diagonal at every small prime, *and* be injective.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.RankTwo

open Finset

/-- `(A, B)` is a prime-difference pair above `m`: every difference `a - b` is,
in absolute value, a prime exceeding `m`. -/
def PrimeDiffPair (A B : Finset ℤ) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, (a - b).natAbs.Prime ∧ m < (a - b).natAbs

/-- A prime difference exceeding `m ≥ ℓ` cannot be divisible by the prime `ℓ`. -/
theorem residues_ne_of_primeDiff {ℓ m : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) {a b : ℤ}
    (h : (a - b).natAbs.Prime ∧ m < (a - b).natAbs) : (a : ZMod ℓ) ≠ (b : ZMod ℓ) := by
  intro hab
  have hdvd : (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ a - b := by
    rw [← ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
    push_cast
    rw [hab, sub_self]
  have h2 : ℓ ∣ (a - b).natAbs := Int.ofNat_dvd_left.1 hdvd
  have := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hℓ h.1).1 h2
  omega

/-- **Residue classes are disjoint.**  For a prime-difference pair above `m`
and any prime `ℓ ≤ m`, `A` and `B` occupy disjoint residue classes mod `ℓ`. -/
theorem residue_classes_disjoint {A B : Finset ℤ} {m ℓ : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) :
    Disjoint (A.image (fun a : ℤ => (a : ZMod ℓ))) (B.image (fun b : ℤ => (b : ZMod ℓ))) := by
  rw [disjoint_left]
  intro r hrA hrB
  obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 hrA
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hba⟩ := mem_image.1 hrB
  exact residues_ne_of_primeDiff hℓ hm (hAB a ha b hb) hba.symm

/-- **Local residue budget.**  `#(A mod ℓ) + #(B mod ℓ) ≤ ℓ` for every prime
`ℓ ≤ m`. -/
theorem residue_budget {A B : Finset ℤ} {m ℓ : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) :
    (A.image (fun a : ℤ => (a : ZMod ℓ))).card + (B.image (fun b : ℤ => (b : ZMod ℓ))).card
      ≤ ℓ := by
  haveI : NeZero ℓ := ⟨hℓ.ne_zero⟩
  rw [← card_union_of_disjoint (residue_classes_disjoint hAB hℓ hm)]
  calc _ ≤ (univ : Finset (ZMod ℓ)).card := card_le_univ _
    _ = ℓ := by rw [card_univ, ZMod.card]

/-- **Parity rigidity (`ℓ = 2`).**  If `B` is nonempty and `(A, B)` is a
prime-difference pair above `m ≥ 2`, then any two elements of `A` have the same
parity. -/
theorem parity_rigidity {A B : Finset ℤ} {m : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m) (hm : 2 ≤ m)
    (hB : B.Nonempty) {a a' : ℤ} (ha : a ∈ A) (ha' : a' ∈ A) : Even (a - a') := by
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hB
  have h1 := residues_ne_of_primeDiff Nat.prime_two hm (hAB a ha b hb)
  have h2 := residues_ne_of_primeDiff Nat.prime_two hm (hAB a' ha' b hb)
  -- in `ZMod 2`, two elements different from the same `b` are equal
  have key : (a : ZMod 2) = (a' : ZMod 2) := by
    revert h1 h2
    generalize (a : ZMod 2) = x
    generalize (a' : ZMod 2) = y
    generalize (b : ZMod 2) = z
    revert x y z
    decide
  have : ((a - a' : ℤ) : ZMod 2) = 0 := by push_cast; rw [key, sub_self]
  rw [ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] at this
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.2 (by exact_mod_cast this)

/-- **Capacity: no slack.**  If every element of `T` is an absolute difference
`|a - b|` with `a ∈ A`, `b ∈ B`, then `|T| ≤ |A|·|B|`. -/
theorem prime_cover_capacity (A B : Finset ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ t ∈ T, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (a - b).natAbs = t) :
    T.card ≤ A.card * B.card := by
  classical
  have hsub : T ⊆ (A ×ˢ B).image (fun x : ℤ × ℤ => (x.1 - x.2).natAbs) := by
    intro t ht
    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩ := hT t ht
    exact mem_image.2 ⟨(a, b), mem_product.2 ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
  calc T.card ≤ _ := card_le_card hsub
    _ ≤ (A ×ˢ B).card := card_image_le
    _ = A.card * B.card := card_product A B

/-- **Tight capacity forces injectivity.**  If `|T| = |A|·|B|` in the setting
of `prime_cover_capacity`, then distinct pairs give distinct differences. -/
theorem tight_capacity_injective (A B : Finset ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ t ∈ T, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (a - b).natAbs = t)
    (htight : T.card = A.card * B.card) :
    Set.InjOn (fun x : ℤ × ℤ => (x.1 - x.2).natAbs) (A ×ˢ B : Finset (ℤ × ℤ)) := by
  classical
  have hsub : T ⊆ (A ×ˢ B).image (fun x : ℤ × ℤ => (x.1 - x.2).natAbs) := by
    intro t ht
    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩ := hT t ht
    exact mem_image.2 ⟨(a, b), mem_product.2 ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
  have h1 := card_le_card hsub
  have h2 : ((A ×ˢ B).image (fun x : ℤ × ℤ => (x.1 - x.2).natAbs)).card
      = (A ×ˢ B).card := by
    apply le_antisymm card_image_le
    rw [card_product, ← htight]; exact h1
  exact card_image_iff.1 h2

/-! ## Lab notes (kernel-checked)

`A = {0, 6}`, `B = {-5, -11}`: the four differences `5, 11, 11, 17` are prime
(above `m = 3`); the cover is *not* injective (`11` twice).  Residues: mod `2`,
`A ↦ {0}`, `B ↦ {1}`; mod `3`, `A ↦ {0}`, `B ↦ {1}` — disjoint as predicted. -/

example : ((({0, 6} : Finset ℤ) ×ˢ ({-5, -11} : Finset ℤ)).image
    (fun x : ℤ × ℤ => (x.1 - x.2).natAbs)) = {5, 11, 17} := by decide

end FactoringFrontier.RankTwo

import Mathlib

/-!
# Symmetric-readout vacuity and the exact `1/2` which-factor wall

Standing finding 6 of the campaign ("for an unordered secret and an
order-sensitive label, every public-input readout is blind") and the
"exact which-factor wall" of the Galois side-channel closure are made precise
here as a *counting* theorem, with an attaining decoder.

Setting: a finite secret set `S`, an involution `σ` of `S` (e.g. swapping the
two prime factors), a public readout `R` with `R ∘ σ = R` (e.g. `N = p·q`), and
a label `L` with `L (σ x) ≠ L x` (e.g. "the first factor").

* `which_factor_wall`: **every** decoder `D` is correct on at most half of `S`:
  `2 · #{x ∈ S | D (R x) = L x} ≤ #S`.
* `symmetric_readout_vacuity`: in particular no decoder is correct on all of a
  nonempty `S`.
* `semiprime_which_factor_wall`: the instance `S = ` ordered pairs of distinct
  primes from a finite set `P`, `R (p,q) = p q`, `L (p,q) = p`.
* `minFac_attains_wall`: the decoder `N ↦ N.minFac` is correct on **exactly**
  half of `S`, so the wall `1/2` is sharp.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.WhichFactor

open Finset

section Abstract

variable {X Y Z : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Z]

/-- **The which-factor wall.**  Under a readout invariant under an involution
that flips the label, any decoder succeeds on at most half of the secrets. -/
theorem which_factor_wall (S : Finset X) (σ : X → X) (hσS : ∀ x ∈ S, σ x ∈ S)
    (hinv : ∀ x, σ (σ x) = x) (R : X → Y) (hR : ∀ x, R (σ x) = R x)
    (L : X → Z) (hL : ∀ x ∈ S, L (σ x) ≠ L x) (D : Y → Z) :
    2 * (S.filter (fun x => D (R x) = L x)).card ≤ S.card := by
  set T := S.filter (fun x => D (R x) = L x) with hT
  have hinj : Set.InjOn σ (T : Set X) := fun x _ y _ hxy => by
    rw [← hinv x, ← hinv y, hxy]
  have himg_card : (T.image σ).card = T.card := card_image_of_injOn hinj
  have hdisj : Disjoint T (T.image σ) := by
    rw [disjoint_left]
    intro x hxT hxI
    obtain ⟨y, hyT, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 hxI
    have hy := (mem_filter.1 hyT)
    have hx := (mem_filter.1 hxT)
    -- `D (R (σ y)) = D (R y) = L y`, but also `= L (σ y)`
    apply hL y hy.1
    rw [← hx.2, hR, hy.2]
  have hsub : T ∪ T.image σ ⊆ S := by
    intro x hx
    rcases mem_union.1 hx with h | h
    · exact (mem_filter.1 h).1
    · obtain ⟨y, hyT, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 h
      exact hσS y (mem_filter.1 hyT).1
  have := card_le_card hsub
  rw [card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, himg_card] at this
  omega

/-- **Symmetric-readout vacuity.**  On a nonempty secret set, no decoder of a
symmetric readout recovers an order-sensitive label everywhere. -/
theorem symmetric_readout_vacuity (S : Finset X) (hS : S.Nonempty) (σ : X → X)
    (hσS : ∀ x ∈ S, σ x ∈ S) (hinv : ∀ x, σ (σ x) = x) (R : X → Y)
    (hR : ∀ x, R (σ x) = R x) (L : X → Z) (hL : ∀ x ∈ S, L (σ x) ≠ L x) (D : Y → Z) :
    ¬ ∀ x ∈ S, D (R x) = L x := by
  intro hall
  have hw := which_factor_wall S σ hσS hinv R hR L hL D
  rw [filter_true_of_mem hall] at hw
  have := hS.card_pos
  omega

end Abstract

section Semiprime

/-- Ordered pairs of distinct elements of `P`. -/
def orderedPairs (P : Finset ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := P.offDiag

/-- **Semiprime which-factor wall.**  For any decoder `D : ℕ → ℕ`, the number of
ordered pairs `(p, q)` of distinct elements of `P` with `D (p q) = p` is at most
half the number of pairs. -/
theorem semiprime_which_factor_wall (P : Finset ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => D (x.1 * x.2) = x.1)).card
      ≤ (orderedPairs P).card := by
  refine which_factor_wall (orderedPairs P) Prod.swap ?_ (fun x => Prod.swap_swap x)
    (fun x => x.1 * x.2) (fun x => Nat.mul_comm _ _) Prod.fst ?_ D
  · intro x hx
    simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx ⊢
    exact ⟨hx.2.1, hx.1, fun h => hx.2.2 h.symm⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx
    exact fun h => hx.2.2 h.symm

/-- The ordered pairs split evenly into increasing and decreasing ones. -/
theorem two_mul_card_lt_pairs (P : Finset ℕ) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => x.1 < x.2)).card = (orderedPairs P).card := by
  set U := (orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => x.1 < x.2)
  set W := (orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => ¬ x.1 < x.2)
  have hsplit := card_filter_add_card_filter_not
    (s := orderedPairs P) (fun x : ℕ × ℕ => x.1 < x.2)
  have hW : W = U.image Prod.swap := by
    ext x
    simp only [W, U, orderedPairs, mem_filter, mem_offDiag, mem_image]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3⟩, h4⟩
      refine ⟨x.swap, ⟨⟨h2, h1, fun h => h3 h.symm⟩, ?_⟩, Prod.swap_swap x⟩
      simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
      omega
    · rintro ⟨y, ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3⟩, h4⟩, rfl⟩
      simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
      exact ⟨⟨h2, h1, fun h => h3 h.symm⟩, by omega⟩
  have hWc : W.card = U.card := by
    rw [hW]; exact card_image_of_injective _ Prod.swap_injective
  change U.card + W.card = _ at hsplit
  omega

/-- **The wall is sharp.**  If `P` consists of primes, the decoder
`N ↦ N.minFac` is correct on exactly half of the ordered pairs. -/
theorem minFac_attains_wall (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => (x.1 * x.2).minFac = x.1)).card
      = (orderedPairs P).card := by
  rw [← two_mul_card_lt_pairs P]
  congr 2
  apply filter_congr
  intro x hx
  simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx
  obtain ⟨hp, hq, hne⟩ := hx
  have hpP := hP _ hp
  have hqP := hP _ hq
  -- the least prime factor of `p q` is `min p q`
  have hmin : (x.1 * x.2).minFac = min x.1 x.2 := by
    have hdvd : (x.1 * x.2).minFac ∣ x.1 * x.2 := Nat.minFac_dvd _
    have hpr : (x.1 * x.2).minFac.Prime :=
      Nat.minFac_prime (by nlinarith [hpP.two_le, hqP.two_le] : 1 < x.1 * x.2).ne'
    rcases (Nat.Prime.dvd_mul hpr).1 hdvd with h | h
    · have e1 := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hpr hpP).1 h
      have le2 : (x.1 * x.2).minFac ≤ x.2 :=
        Nat.minFac_le_of_dvd hqP.two_le (Dvd.intro_left _ rfl)
      rw [e1] at le2 ⊢; exact (min_eq_left le2).symm
    · have e1 := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hpr hqP).1 h
      have le2 : (x.1 * x.2).minFac ≤ x.1 :=
        Nat.minFac_le_of_dvd hpP.two_le (Dvd.intro _ rfl)
      rw [e1] at le2 ⊢; exact (min_eq_right le2).symm
  rw [hmin]
  constructor
  · intro h; rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h' | h'
    · exact h'
    · rw [min_eq_right h'.le] at h; omega
  · intro h; exact min_eq_left h.le

/-! ## Lab notes (kernel-checked)

`P = {2,3,5,7}`: `12` ordered pairs; the `minFac` decoder is right on the `6`
increasing ones; the "max factor" decoder `N ↦ N / N.minFac` on the other `6`. -/

example : 2 * ((orderedPairs {2, 3, 5, 7}).filter
    (fun x => (x.1 * x.2).minFac = x.1)).card = 12 := by
  rw [minFac_attains_wall]
  · decide
  · intro p hp
    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hp
    rcases hp with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> norm_num

example : (orderedPairs {2, 3, 5, 7}).card = 12 := by decide

end Semiprime

end FactoringFrontier.WhichFactor

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Numerical companion to "Four Walls Around Factoring".

Demonstrates, on concrete numbers, the four theorems of the paper:

  1. The multi-polynomial split-set theorem: for a prime p not dividing a,
     p divides some value of (a x + b)^2 - N  iff  N is a square mod p,
     for every choice of (a, b); the column density is exactly (p-1)/2.
  2. The Pythagorean leg channel: every triple N^2 + b^2 = c^2 with b > 0 and
     c - b != 1 reveals a nontrivial factor gcd(c - b, N); for odd N,
     N is composite iff such a triple exists.  Also checks the conjectured
     count (tau(N^2) - 1)/2 of leg triples for odd N.
  3. The which-factor wall: with readout N = p q (symmetric) and label "the
     first factor" (order-sensitive), every decoder is right on at most half
     of the ordered pairs; the least-prime-factor decoder attains exactly half.
  4. The rank-two local obstruction: if every difference a - b is a prime > m,
     then A and B occupy disjoint residue classes modulo every prime l <= m,
     and |T| <= |A||B| with equality forcing injectivity.

Pure Python 3, standard library only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small number-theory toolkit
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Deterministic trial-division primality test (fine for small n)."""
    if n < 2:
        return False
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return n == 2
    r = math.isqrt(n)
    f = 3
    while f <= r:
        if n % f == 0:
            return False
        f += 2
    return True


def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if n < 2:
        return []
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = 0
    for i in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i, v in enumerate(sieve) if v]


def min_fac(n: int) -> int:
    """Least prime factor of n >= 2."""
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return 2
    f = 3
    while f * f <= n:
        if n % f == 0:
            return f
        f += 2
    return n


def is_square_mod(n: int, p: int) -> bool:
    """Is n a square in Z/pZ (0 counts as a square)?"""
    n %= p
    return any((x * x) % p == n for x in range(p))


def num_divisors(n: int) -> int:
    """tau(n), the number of positive divisors."""
    count = 0
    for d in range(1, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
        if n % d == 0:
            count += 1 if d * d == n else 2
    return count


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Multi-polynomial split set
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_column(N: int, a: int, b: int, p: int) -> bool:
    """Does p divide (a x + b)^2 - N for some integer x?  (one period suffices)"""
    return any(((a * x + b) ** 2 - N) % p == 0 for x in range(p))


def column_set(N: int, polys: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]], factor_base: Iterable[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """Union of the column sets of the family {(a_i x + b_i)^2 - N}, restricted
    to primes coprime to every leading coefficient a_i."""
    out: Set[int] = set()
    for p in factor_base:
        if any(a % p == 0 for a, _ in polys):
            continue
        if any(is_column(N, a, b, p) for a, b in polys):
            out.add(p)
    return out


def split_set(N: int, factor_base: Iterable[int], exclude: Sequence[int] = ()) -> Set[int]:
    """Primes p (not dividing any element of `exclude`) with N a square mod p."""
    return {p for p in factor_base
            if all(e % p != 0 for e in exclude) and is_square_mod(N, p)}


def column_density_count(p: int, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """#{ n in (Z/p)^* : p divides some (a x + b)^2 - n }."""
    return sum(1 for n in range(1, p) if is_column(n, a, b, p))


def demo_split_set() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("1. THE MULTI-POLYNOMIAL COLUMN SET IS THE SPLIT SET")
    print("=" * 72)
    # Lab instance from the paper: p = 7, a = 3, b = 5.
    roots_2 = [x for x in range(7) if ((3 * x + 5) ** 2 - 2) % 7 == 0]
    roots_3 = [x for x in range(7) if ((3 * x + 5) ** 2 - 3) % 7 == 0]
    print(f"p=7, a=3, b=5: roots of (3x+5)^2-2 mod 7 -> {roots_2} "
          f"(2 = 3^2 mod 7 is a square)")
    print(f"               roots of (3x+5)^2-3 mod 7 -> {roots_3} "
          f"(3 is a non-residue mod 7)")
    print(f"   check: 11^2-2 = {11**2-2} = 7*{(11**2-2)//7},  "
          f"17^2-2 = {17**2-2} = 7*{(17**2-2)//7}")

    N = 1000003 * 999983  # a semiprime
    fb = [p for p in primes_up_to(20000) if p > 2 and N % p != 0]
    rng = random.Random(2026)
    family = [(rng.randrange(1, 10 ** 6), rng.randrange(0, 10 ** 6)) for _ in range(6)]
    cols = column_set(N, family, fb)
    split = split_set(N, fb, exclude=[a for a, _ in family])
    print(f"\nN = {N}; factor base = odd primes < 20000 ({len(fb)} primes)")
    print(f"family of {len(family)} random MPQS polynomials (a, b): {family[:3]} ...")
    single = column_set(N, [(1, 0)], fb)
    print(f"column set == split set ?  {cols == split}")
    print(f"family columns == single-polynomial (x^2 - N) columns, on common primes ?  "
          f"{cols == {p for p in single if all(a % p for a, _ in family)}}")
    usable = [p for p in fb if all(a % p for a, _ in family)]
    print(f"column density = {len(cols)}/{len(usable)} = {len(cols)/len(usable):.3f}  "
          f"(theory: ~1/2, NOT ~1/4)")

    print("\nExact density per prime: #{n mod p, n != 0 : p is a column} vs (p-1)/2")
    for p in [3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 101]:
        a, b = rng.randrange(1, p), rng.randrange(0, p)
        c = column_density_count(p, a, b)
        print(f"  p={p:4d}  a={a:3d} b={b:3d}  count={c:3d}   (p-1)/2={(p-1)//2:3d}   "
              f"{'OK' if c == (p - 1) // 2 else 'FAIL'}")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Pythagorean leg channel
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def leg_triples(N: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
    """All (b, c) with N^2 + b^2 = c^2, b > 0, via (c-b)(c+b) = N^2."""
    out: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    N2 = N * N
    for u in range(1, N):
        if N2 % u:
            continue
        v = N2 // u
        if (u + v) % 2 == 0 and u < v:
            out.append(((v - u) // 2, (u + v) // 2))
    return sorted(out, reverse=True)


def factor_from_triple(N: int, b: int, c: int) -> int:
    """The coordinate-gcd channel: gcd(c - b, N)."""
    return math.gcd(c - b, N)


def triple_from_factor(d: int, e: int) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Scaled trivial triple of e = 2m+1 by d: leg d*e, with c - b = d."""
    m = (e - 1) // 2
    return d * e, d * (2 * m * m + 2 * m), d * (2 * m * m + 2 * m + 1)


def demo_pythagorean() -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 72)
    print("2. THE PYTHAGOREAN CHANNEL IS A COORDINATE GCD (AND CIRCULAR)")
    print("=" * 72)
    N = 15
    print(f"Leg N = {N}:")
    for b, c in leg_triples(N):
        g = factor_from_triple(N, b, c)
        tag = "trivial (c-b=1), no information" if c - b == 1 else f"factor {g} revealed"
        print(f"  {N}^2 + {b}^2 = {c}^2   c-b = {c-b:3d}   gcd(c-b,N) = {g}   {tag}")

    print("\nTheorem check: every nontrivial triple yields 1 < gcd < N, for all N in [3, 400]")
    bad = 0
    for N in range(3, 401):
        for b, c in leg_triples(N):
            g = factor_from_triple(N, b, c)
            if c - b != 1 and not (1 < g < N):
                bad += 1
    print(f"  violations: {bad}")

    print("\nOdd N: composite <=> a nontrivial leg triple exists   (checked N in [3, 999])")
    mismatch = 0
    for N in range(3, 1000, 2):
        has_nontriv = any(c - b != 1 for b, c in leg_triples(N))
        if has_nontriv != (not is_prime(N)):
            mismatch += 1
    print(f"  mismatches: {mismatch}")

    print("\nConverse construction from a factorization N = d*e (scaled trivial triple):")
    for d, e in [(3, 5), (7, 11), (101, 103)]:
        L, b, c = triple_from_factor(d, e)
        print(f"  d={d}, e={e}:  {L}^2 + {b}^2 = {c}^2 ? {L*L + b*b == c*c};  c-b = {c-b}")

    print("\nConjecture (open): #leg triples for odd N equals (tau(N^2)-1)/2")
    ok = all(len(leg_triples(N)) == (num_divisors(N * N) - 1) // 2 for N in range(3, 800, 2))
    print(f"  holds for all odd N in [3, 799]: {ok}   (numerical evidence only)")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The which-factor wall
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Decoder = Callable[[int], int]


def decoder_accuracy(P: Sequence[int], D: Decoder) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """(#correct, #pairs) for decoder D guessing p from N = p*q over ordered pairs."""
    pairs = [(p, q) for p in P for q in P if p != q]
    correct = sum(1 for p, q in pairs if D(p * q) == p)
    return correct, len(pairs)


def best_possible_decoder(P: Sequence[int]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Brute-force optimum: for each readout N, choose the best single answer."""
    pairs = [(p, q) for p in P for q in P if p != q]
    by_N: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
    for p, q in pairs:
        by_N.setdefault(p * q, []).append(p)
    best = sum(max(labels.count(z) for z in set(labels)) for labels in by_N.values())
    return best, len(pairs)


def demo_which_factor() -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 72)
    print("3. THE WHICH-FACTOR WALL: NO DECODER BEATS 1/2")
    print("=" * 72)
    P = [2, 3, 5, 7]
    decoders: Dict[str, Decoder] = {
        "least prime factor": min_fac,
        "largest prime factor": lambda n: n // min_fac(n),
        "always 3": lambda n: 3,
    }
    for name, D in decoders.items():
        c, t = decoder_accuracy(P, D)
        print(f"  P={P}  decoder={name:24s}  correct {c}/{t} = {c/t:.3f}")
    rng = random.Random(1)
    P2 = primes_up_to(200)[3:]
    best, tot = best_possible_decoder(P2)
    print(f"\n  P = {len(P2)} primes in [7, 200]: optimal decoder (brute force) "
          f"correct {best}/{tot} = {best/tot:.4f}")
    rand_D: Decoder = lambda n: rng.choice([min_fac(n), n // min_fac(n)])
    c, t = decoder_accuracy(P2, rand_D)
    print(f"  random coin-flip decoder: {c}/{t} = {c/t:.4f}")
    c, t = decoder_accuracy(P2, min_fac)
    print(f"  least-prime-factor decoder: {c}/{t} = {c/t:.4f}  (exactly 1/2: the wall is sharp)")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Rank-two local obstruction
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_prime_diff_pair(A: Sequence[int], B: Sequence[int], m: int) -> bool:
    return all(is_prime(abs(a - b)) and abs(a - b) > m for a in A for b in B)


def residue_report(A: Sequence[int], B: Sequence[int], l: int) -> Tuple[Set[int], Set[int]]:
    return {a % l for a in A}, {b % l for b in B}


def greedy_prime_diff_pair(size: int, m: int, X: int, seed: int = 0) -> Tuple[List[int], List[int]]:
    """Greedy search for A, B in [0, X) with all |a-b| prime > m (small demo)."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    A: List[int] = []
    B: List[int] = []
    cand = list(range(X))
    rng.shuffle(cand)
    for x in cand:
        okA = len(A) < size and all(is_prime(abs(x - b)) and abs(x - b) > m for b in B)
        okB = len(B) < size and all(is_prime(abs(a - x)) and abs(a - x) > m for a in A)
        # always feed the smaller side first, so both sets grow together
        if okB and (len(B) < len(A) or not okA):
            B.append(x)
        elif okA:
            A.append(x)
        if len(A) == size and len(B) == size:
            break
    return sorted(A), sorted(B)


def demo_rank_two() -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 72)
    print("4. RANK-TWO LOCAL OBSTRUCTION: DISJOINT RESIDUES AND NO SLACK")
    print("=" * 72)
    A, B, m = [0, 6], [-5, -11], 3
    diffs = sorted({abs(a - b) for a in A for b in B})
    print(f"A={A}, B={B}: differences {[abs(a-b) for a in A for b in B]} -> set {diffs}")
    print(f"  prime-difference pair above m={m}: {is_prime_diff_pair(A, B, m)}")
    for l in [2, 3]:
        rA, rB = residue_report(A, B, l)
        print(f"  mod {l}: A -> {sorted(rA)}, B -> {sorted(rB)}, disjoint={rA.isdisjoint(rB)}, "
              f"budget {len(rA)}+{len(rB)} <= {l}")
    print(f"  capacity: |T|={len(diffs)} <= |A||B|={len(A)*len(B)} ; not tight, "
          f"and indeed 11 appears twice (not injective)")

    m = 7
    A, B = greedy_prime_diff_pair(size=5, m=m, X=3000, seed=4)
    print(f"\nGreedy search, m={m}: A={A}\n                      B={B}")
    print(f"  prime-difference pair: {is_prime_diff_pair(A, B, m)}")
    for l in [p for p in primes_up_to(m)]:
        rA, rB = residue_report(A, B, l)
        print(f"  mod {l}: #A-classes={len(rA)}, #B-classes={len(rB)}, "
              f"disjoint={rA.isdisjoint(rB)}, sum={len(rA)+len(rB)} <= {l}")
    T = {abs(a - b) for a in A for b in B}
    print(f"  |T| = {len(T)} <= |A||B| = {len(A)*len(B)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo_split_set()
    demo_pythagorean()
    demo_which_factor()
    demo_rank_two()

# Computational Evidence — Factoring Frontier cycle

Script: `scripts/factoring_frontier_evidence.py` (plain Python, no dependencies).
These are exploratory checks; the claims themselves are proved in Lean in
`Catalog/Applications/FactoringFrontier/`. Small instances are also
kernel-checked inside the Lean files ("Lab notes" sections).

## 1. MPQS column set = single-polynomial split set
For each odd prime `p < 2000` not dividing `N`, a random MPQS polynomial
`(a x + b)^2 − N` with `p ∤ a` was tested over one full period, and the hit
set was compared with the Euler criterion `N^{(p−1)/2} ≡ 1 (mod p)`.

| N | primes tested | agreement | split density |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10403 = 101·103 | 300 | 300/300 | 0.493 |
| 1000036000099 = 1000003·1000033 | 302 | 302/302 | 0.513 |
| 2147483645 | 300 | 300/300 | 0.507 |

No counterexample. Density about 1/2 matches `mpqs_column_density`
(exactly `(p−1)/2` residues per prime). The record's earlier "~1/4" value is not
reproduced.

## 2. Pythagorean triples with leg N
All triples `N^2 + b^2 = c^2` with `b > 0`, listed as `(c−b, b, c, gcd(c−b, N))`:

* `N = 15`: (1,112,113,**1**), (3,36,39,3), (5,20,25,5), (9,8,17,3)
* `N = 77`: (1,2964,2965,**1**), (7,420,427,7), (11,264,275,11), (49,36,85,7)
* `N = 9`: (1,40,41,**1**), (3,12,15,3)
* `N = 105`: 13 triples; every one with `c−b ≠ 1` has gcd in {3,5,7,15,21,35}.

Every triple with `c − b ≠ 1` gives a nontrivial gcd, and `c − b = 1` always gives
gcd 1. This matches `leg_triple_gcd_nontrivial` exactly, with no counterexample.
The triple count equals `(τ(N^2) − 1)/2`: 4 for `pq`, 13 for `105`. This count
is observed only, not proved.

## 3. Which-factor wall
Primes below 60 give 17 primes and 272 ordered pairs. The `minFac` decoder is
correct on 136 = 272/2 of them. This matches `minFac_attains_wall` (exactly
half) and `semiprime_which_factor_wall` (no decoder does better).

## 4. Rank-2 local obstruction
`A = {0,6}`, `B = {−5,−11}`: the differences are 5, 11, 11 and 17, all prime.
Mod 2 and mod 3 the residues of `A` and `B` are disjoint, and the cover is not
injective. This instance is kernel-checked in `RankTwoLocalObstruction.lean`.

The leg-triple count `(τ(N²)−1)/2` for odd `N` is the number of ways to write `N` as
a leg (OEIS A046079, "number of Pythagorean triangles with leg n"). This

# Summary of changes for run 805f68e0-f940-436e-b874-c8391989cb79
I wrote all five deliverables, then committed, pushed and published them. `demo.py`, the four algorithm scripts and the four interactive widgets run and give the numbers quoted in the papers. Two things were only partly checked: `RESEARCH_PAPER.tex` could not be compiled here (no offline LaTeX setup), and the four plotting scripts could not draw images (matplotlib is not installed).

All three prose documents are self-contained and make no reference to formal-proof tooling, file paths or code names. Each states and proves four results:

- **Split sets:** if a prime \(p\) does not divide \(a\), then \(p\) divides some \((ax+b)^2-N\) exactly when \(N\) is a square mod \(p\). So no choice of sieve polynomials changes which primes can appear, and the column density is exactly \((p-1)/2\) out of \(p-1\), not \(1/4\).
- **Pythagorean legs:** a triple \(N^2+b^2=c^2\) with \(b>0\) and \(c-b\ne1\) gives a factor \(\gcd(c-b,N)\). For odd \(N\), \(N\) is composite exactly when such a triple exists, so the shortcut is circular.
- **Which factor:** from a symmetric readout such as \(N=pq\), no decoder names the first factor correctly more than half the time, and "output the least prime factor" reaches exactly \(1/2\).
- **Rank-two covers:** if every difference \(a-b\) is a prime above \(m\), then \(A\) and \(B\) use disjoint residue classes mod every prime \(\ell\le m\). Also \(|T|\le|A||B|\), and equality forces every pair to give a different prime.

**The deliverables:**
- **`ARTICLE.md`** (about 2,600 words): a popular account built around the four results, plus the wider campaign findings, the corrections to the record and the three open problems.
- **`RESEARCH_PAPER.md`** (about 5,500 words): abstract, the summary table of verdicts, the general principles, the record corrections, definitions, full statements with proofs, algorithms, experiments, discussion and future directions.
- **`RESEARCH_PAPER.tex`**: an amsart version of the same paper with inline theorem environments. Since it could not be compiled, I checked it by script instead: environments pair up, braces and math delimiters balance, and every cross-reference has a matching label.
- **`demo.py`**: standard library only, runs in about 14 seconds. It checks:
  - **Split sets:** the column set equals the split set on the semiprime 1000003·999983, using 2261 odd primes below 20000.
  - **Pythagorean legs:** all triples on leg 15; the gcd result for every \(N\le400\); and "composite exactly when a triple exists" for every odd \(N\le999\).
  - **Which factor:** the best possible decoder over 43 primes scores exactly 1/2.
  - **Rank-two covers:** a greedy search finds a 5×5 pair whose 25 differences are 25 distinct primes.
  - **Leg-triple count:** the conjectured count \((\tau(N^2)-1)/2\) holds for odd \(N\le799\). This is numerical evidence only.
- **`PACKAGE.json`**: all metadata fields plus the content below.
  - **Article, paper and demo:** the full text of each.

# Future Directions — after the Factoring Frontier cycle

This cycle produced four machine-checked results (0 sorries), all in
`Catalog/Applications/FactoringFrontier/`:

* **MultiPolySplitSet** — the MPQS column set is the single-polynomial split
  set for *every* polynomial family (`family_columns_iff`), and its density is
  exactly `(p−1)/2` (`mpqs_column_density`). This proves the record correction
  "~1/4 → 1/2".
* **PythagoreanLegChannel** — for every `N > 1`, each Pythagorean triple with leg `N`
  and `c−b ≠ 1` reveals a nontrivial factor as `gcd(c−b, N)`. For odd `N`,
  composite ⇔ there is a nontrivial leg triple. So the channel is circular.
* **WhichFactorWall** — under any symmetric readout, every decoder of an
  order-sensitive label is correct on at most 1/2 of the secrets, and `minFac`
  reaches exactly 1/2.
* **RankTwoLocalObstruction** — any prime-difference pair `(A,B)` must keep
  disjoint residue classes mod every small prime (`#A mod ℓ + #B mod ℓ ≤ ℓ`), and
  a tight `n^{2/3}` cover must be injective.

## 1. Residue-box sieve bound for rank-2 prime covers
**Conjecture.** If `A − B` consists of primes greater than `m`, then
`|A|·|B| ≤ C · X^2 / (log X)^2` for `A, B ⊂ [1, X]`. The `n^{2/3}`-from-`n^{1/3}`
rank-2 door therefore cannot be reached with `|A| = |B| = n^{1/3}` inside an
interval of length `n^{1/3+o(1)}`.
The key insight is that `residue_budget` gives a product of local densities
`∏_{ℓ≤m}(1 − ω_ℓ/ℓ)`, the setting of a two-dimensional Selberg sieve.
Why now? The local obstruction is now a theorem, so only the global sieve step
remains.

## 2. Exact leg-triple count as a divisor function
**Conjecture.** For odd `N`, the number of triples `N² + b² = c²` with `b > 0` is
exactly `(τ(N²) − 1)/2`. The number with `gcd(c−b, N) = 1` is always exactly one.
The key insight is that `leg_factor_identity` turns triples into ordered
factorisations `u·v = N²` with `u < v`, and for odd `N` the parity condition is automatic.
Why now? Both directions of the bijection are already in Lean.

## 3. Which-factor wall for k-factor secrets
**Conjecture.** For secrets that are ordered `k`-tuples of distinct primes,
readout = product, and label = the first coordinate, every decoder is correct on
at most a `1/k` fraction. `minFac` attains exactly `1/k`.
The key insight is that the symmetric group `S_k` acts freely on these tuples
while preserving the readout, so the involution argument becomes an orbit argument.
Why now? The `k = 2` case (`which_factor_wall`) is proved with an attaining
decoder.

## 4. Number-field analogue of the multi-polynomial split set
**Conjecture.** For NFS with a fixed degree-`d` polynomial `f`, changing the
linear-polynomial family `a − bθ` does not change the set of degree-one prime
ideals that can appear. That set is exactly `{p : f has a root mod p}`, and its density
is `1/|G|·#{σ ∈ G with a fixed point}`.
The key insight is the same unit-shift argument as `exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare`,
applied to a root of `f` instead of a square root of `N`.
Why now? The quadratic case (`d = 2`) is now a theorem, and it is the template.
